An intrinsic hallucination contradicts the supplied evidence; an extrinsic one adds a claim not supported by it, even if that claim happens to be true elsewhere. Split the response into atomic claims, retrieve each claim's evidence, and use entailment/contradiction scoring with an explicit unsupported category. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15217) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685)

For example, a passage reporting revenue of 10 million does not support a claim about profit, and contradicts revenue of 20 million for the same period. Negation, dates, arithmetic, and incomplete context need dedicated checks. A compact NLI model, batching, caching, and short evidence windows can reduce latency, but “under 20 ms” depends on hardware and workload. Measure end-to-end tail latency and calibrated error rates; abstain when evidence is insufficient.
